app_purpose: Python async HTTP server/client library; its server-side pure-Python HTTP request parser frames requests (used behind proxies -> request-smuggling surface)

v0.ref: aiohttp v3.8.5 http_parser.py get_content_length(): `try: length = int(length_hdr) except ValueError: raise InvalidHeader`. int() accepts '+0'/'1_0'/sign AND Unicode digits.

v1.ref: aiohttp v3.8.6 http_parser.py get_content_length(): `if not length_hdr.strip(' \t').isdecimal(): raise InvalidHeader(CONTENT_LENGTH); return int(length_hdr)`. CVE-2023-47627 fix (commit d5c12ba890557a575c313bb3017910d7616fce3d). INCOMPLETE: str.isdecimal() is True for any Unicode decimal digit, so a Unicode-digit Content-Length is still accepted -> CVE-2024-23829.

v2.ref: aiohttp v3.9.2 http_parser.py get_content_length(): `if not DIGITS.fullmatch(length_hdr): raise InvalidHeader` where DIGITS = re.compile(r'\d+', re.ASCII). CVE-2024-23829 fix (commit 33ccdfb0a12690af5bb49bda2319ec0907fa7827). re.ASCII restricts \d to [0-9] -> Unicode-digit CL rejected.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2024-23829 (GHSA-8qpw-xqxj-h4r2): 'aiohttp's HTTP parser (the python one, not llhttp) still overly lenient about separators' -- this vulnerability exists due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2023-47627. Security-sensitive parts of the Python HTTP parser retained minor differences in allowable character sets (e.g. Unicode digits accepted where only ASCII digits are standards-compliant).

labels.residual_class: unicode-digit-leniency (ASCII-only guard missing: str.isdecimal accepts non-ASCII decimal digits that int() then parses)
